items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (e.g. 9/12/2025 and 6/22/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, coronary atherosclerosis with old MI 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant is currently ordered: the brief inpatient dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban orders all ended in January-February 2025 and current outpatient medications are only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027, continuous since 10/2/2023) at a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised for QT safety. Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 491 ms and RR 856 ms, Bazett QTc about 531 ms, compared with about 411 ms before citalopram (6/17/2020). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) is a current order (6/17/2026-1/6/2027) and has been continuous since 2022. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 572 ms and RR 1042 ms, Bazett QTc about 561 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold (the 4/6/2022 tracing in atrial fibrillation had a QTc of about 446 ms). Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal, so amiodarone is the likely cause. Prescriber review is required; a current ECG would also be reasonable given how old the last tracing is.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 11/10/2025. Because the start date is on/after 9/1/2025 but before 3/1/2026, the original memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was obtained on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG shows QTc about 542 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, satisfying the requirement (sinus rhythm, QTc about 459 ms).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 3/2/2026. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, meeting the requirement (sinus rhythm, QTc about 375 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 4/10/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. No ECG was obtained within that window; the only tracing (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start, i.e. outside the required time. The requirement was therefore not met by its due date, which has long passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/1/2026 (the only earlier exposure was a brief peri-operative inpatient order in December 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. Her only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025; no tracing has been obtained since the start, and the due date passed before the 9/24/2026 review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/10/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG exists in the clinic record, but the 8/25/2026 telephone note reports that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025), but as of the 9/24/2026 review the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/1/2026 the clinician documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR', and a new warfarin order was written the same day. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a dose change, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with documented paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation (coded AF conditions and 'paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, atrial fibrillation' in every clinic note through 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy = 1, essential hypertension = 1); age <65 and no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease. Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the only warfarin orders were brief inpatient courses in March and June 2025; current outpatient medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD - permitted to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a dose change, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is from 6/17/2026 (2.7); no INR has been resulted since the dose change and the due date passed one week before the 9/24/2026 review.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and listed in the cardiology clinic history at every visit through 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1). Anticoagulation is recommended, but no anticoagulant has ever been prescribed - current medications are levothyroxine (and previously tamsulosin) only. The prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (2025 admission) should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulant with a CHA2DS2-VASc of 3 needs review.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2, female 1). She has a very high stroke risk yet no anticoagulant: current medications are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine; the only antithrombotic ever ordered was clopidogrel in March 2025, which is not adequate for AF-related stroke prevention.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (valid through 1/4/2027) and remains current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting/continuing an anticoagulant after a major GI bleed that was explicitly held 'pending cardiology review' requires prescriber review.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was 'switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage', and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026); however rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and was never stopped, and the note's own medication list contains both apixaban and rivaroxaban. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban (plus clopidogrel) carries a major bleeding risk and must be reconciled.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves at a ventricular rate of about 132-136/min (RR intervals 346-718 ms and 348-650 ms) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, matching her coded 'unspecified atrial fibrillation'. Neither the rhythm nor the rate documented in the note is supported by the same-day tracings.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) is a current order (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 487 ms and RR 880 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. The 5/14/2024 note calling that tracing 'QT acceptable' is not supported by the tracing. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 3/18/2026) are essentially normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, started 11/10/2025 and currently ordered 7/12/2026-1/9/2027) in a man also on warfarin, clopidogrel and aspirin. His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 533 ms with RR 968 ms, Bazett QTc about 542 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold, and markedly increased from the QTc of about 411 ms on the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

interpretations.explanation: Cardiology-clinic ECG of 3/7/2026. Regular P wave before every QRS, upright in II/III/aVF and biphasic in V1, with a constant PR of about 180 ms - sinus rhythm at 81/min with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 658-856 ms). QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal), QT 323 ms with RR 744 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 375 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. The same-day clinic note stating sinus rhythm is concordant.

7/15/2025. Regular rhythm at 104/min (RR 568-586 ms) with a prominent upright P wave in II (0.22 mV) before each QRS, PR about 135 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +20 to +40 degrees (normal), QT 339 ms at RR 579 ms giving QTc about 446 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with a narrow QRS, marked ST depression and inverted T waves and a short QT (QTc of roughly 340-360 ms); the QTc is now more than 60 ms longer as the rate has slowed and the T waves have become upright.

5/21/2024. Regular rhythm at 108/min (RR 538-614 ms) with an upright P wave in II/I before each QRS and a constant PR of about 115 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal), QT 327 ms at RR 548 ms giving QTc about 442 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

6/10/2026 (19:36). Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia, RR 348-650 ms with a mean of about 440 ms (mean rate about 136/min), no organised P waves and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about 0 to +5 degrees (normal), QT 292 ms at a median RR of 418 ms giving QTc about 452 ms. The prior tracing recorded 2 hours earlier the same evening shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 132/min with an identical QRS and QTc, so there is no interval change. (Note: the clinic note of the same day describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' is contradicted by both tracings.)

8/2/2025. Very regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 864-884 ms) with a small, reproducible atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 150 ms (low-amplitude P, most visible in III/aVL; P axis is leftward/superior). QRS 72 ms, frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal), QT 397 ms at RR 872 ms giving QTc about 425 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block; the high-frequency deflections coincide with the QRS itself and are not pacing spikes. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 shows the same regular rhythm at 61/min with a QTc of about 400 ms; the QRS polarity in the limb leads is reversed on that tracing (probable arm-lead reversal), but there is no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

5/23/2024. Regular rhythm at 98/min (RR 596-628 ms) with upright P waves in II (0.17 mV) and negative P in V1 before every QRS, PR about 115 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +4 degrees (normal), QT 307 ms at RR 616 ms giving QTc about 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

12/25/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 72/min (RR 820-840 ms) with a low-amplitude upright P wave in I/II before each QRS and a PR of about 135 ms. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +20 degrees (normal), QT 372 ms at RR 832 ms giving QTc about 408 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

11/15/2024. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 694-1164 ms, RMSSD 288 ms) with no P waves - the pre-QRS segment is flat and non-reproducible between beats (correlation -0.07) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with a controlled/slow ventricular response, mean rate about 61/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +25 degrees (normal), QT 417 ms at a median RR of 1128 ms giving QTc about 392 ms. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves (0.21 mV in II) and a PR of about 175 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new since that study; intervals are otherwise unchanged.

3/9/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 58/min (RR 976-1082 ms) with tall upright P waves in II/aVF and a PR of about 110-115 ms. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal), QT 422 ms at RR 1030 ms giving QTc about 416 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 is essentially identical (sinus 62/min, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 437 ms); no significant change.

8/23/2025. Very regular sinus rhythm at 83/min (RR 716-726 ms) with an upright P wave in II before every QRS and a PR of about 140 ms. QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees (normal), QT 333 ms at RR 720 ms giving QTc about 393 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

6/19/2020. Regular sinus rhythm at 76/min (RR 774-804 ms) with prominent upright P waves in II (0.26 mV) and a PR of about 155 ms. QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal), QT 400 ms at RR 783 ms giving QTc about 452 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2/2/2020 (sinus 75/min, QRS 74 ms, flat/inverted T waves with QTc about 505 ms) the T waves are now upright and the QTc is about 50 ms shorter - less than the 60 ms threshold, so no significant interval change is reported.

1/18/2021. Metronomically regular rhythm (RR 494-502 ms) at 120/min with an upright P wave in II/aVF before every QRS (0.20 mV) and a constant PR of about 160 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +48 degrees (normal), QT 274 ms with RR 498 ms giving QTc about 389 ms. No bundle branch block, no AV block. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc about 397 ms) the morphology and intervals are essentially unchanged; no significant change.

6/23/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 55/min (RR 1074-1116 ms). An upright P wave precedes every QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 210-220 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 80 ms (deep Q waves inferiorly with a dominant R in V1-V2), frontal axis about +10 to +40 degrees (normal), QT 391 ms at RR 1103 ms giving QTc about 372 ms. No bundle branch block; the high-frequency deflections coincide with the R peak and are QRS-related, not pacing spikes. The prior tracing of 11/30/2024 is similar (sinus 51/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 356 ms); no significant change.

9/13/2025. Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia, RR 290-580 ms (mean about 397 ms, rate about 151/min) with a completely flat pre-QRS baseline and no reproducible atrial activity (beat-to-beat correlation -0.05) - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about -10 to -19 degrees (normal), QT 271 ms at a median RR of 394 ms giving QTc about 431 ms. The prior ECG of 9/12/2025 showed a regular rhythm at about 77/min with discernible P waves and a PR of about 135 ms (one premature beat), so the atrial fibrillation is new.

11/23/2025. Sinus rhythm at 72/min (RR 788-922 ms) with upright P waves in II (0.21 mV) and a PR of about 170 ms. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +10 degrees (normal), QT 354 ms at RR 818 ms giving QTc about 392 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 showed the same sinus rhythm at 67/min but with a much later, broader T wave: QT 496 ms at RR 892 ms, QTc about 526 ms. The QTc has therefore shortened by well over 60 ms. The same-day clinic note describing sinus rhythm is concordant with this tracing.

2/15/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 74/min (RR 780-828 ms) with an upright P wave before each QRS and a PR of about 180 ms (not prolonged beyond 200 ms). QRS 86 ms with a qR pattern in I/aVL and prominent R in aVF, frontal axis about +37 to +52 degrees (normal), QT 379 ms at RR 814 ms giving QTc about 420 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

6/26/2023. Very regular rhythm at 112/min (RR 536-542 ms) with a discrete upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) and biphasic P in V1 before every QRS, PR about 160-175 ms - sinus tachycardia, not atrial flutter (a single atrial deflection per cycle with a clearly isoelectric TP segment). QRS 90 ms with very deep S waves in V1-V2 and tall R in V5-V6 (voltage criteria for LVH), frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal), QT 291 ms at RR 538 ms giving QTc about 396 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 is essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc about 388 ms); no change.

3/14/2025. Underlying rhythm is regular at about 61/min (RR 956-998 ms) with a low-amplitude upright P wave before each QRS at a PR of about 195 ms; there is one premature beat (RR 538 ms) followed by a compensatory pause (1370 ms), which accounts for the apparent RR variability - sinus rhythm with a premature atrial/ventricular complex rather than atrial fibrillation. QRS 94 ms with an rS pattern inferiorly, frontal axis about -23 to -30 degrees (normal/borderline left), QT 370 ms at a median RR of 980 ms giving QTc about 373 ms. PR is not beyond 200 ms, so no AV block is reported. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

4/29/2026. Regular rhythm at 70/min (RR 836-884 ms) with a reproducible P wave before every QRS at a constant PR of about 140 ms - sinus rhythm. The limb leads are globally inverted (net QRS -1.28 mV in I, +1.00 mV in aVR, P wave negative in I and II), giving a computed frontal axis of about -172 degrees, i.e. an extreme (north-west) axis; this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal and repeat tracing with correct lead placement would be reasonable. QRS 88 ms, QT 352 ms at RR 866 ms giving QTc about 378 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

11/10/2023. Sinus rhythm at 70/min (RR 800-892 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS and a PR of about 150 ms. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +42 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is prolonged with a late, broad, low-amplitude T wave: QT 491 ms at RR 856 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 531 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132/min with a QTc of about 411 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms - consistent with citalopram 40 mg daily started in October 2023 and flagged as a QT safety issue.

3/8/2026. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 858-906 ms) with an upright P wave in II/aVF before each QRS and a PR of about 145 ms. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal), QT 431 ms at RR 881 ms giving QTc about 459 ms - prolonged but below the 500 ms review threshold for his escitalopram. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

1/13/2019. Regular rhythm at 53/min (RR 1112-1170 ms) with an upright P wave in II (0.18 mV) before every QRS and a PR of about 175 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about -6 degrees (normal), QT 380 ms at RR 1136 ms giving QTc about 357 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 12/13/2018 showed sinus rhythm at 66/min with a PR of about 190 ms, QRS 92 ms and QTc about 383 ms; no significant change.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 862-902 ms), upright P in II/aVF and negative in V1 with PR about 134 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: a long flat ST segment with a late, low, broad T wave; QT 487 ms at RR 880 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 had a QTc of about 355 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms - consistent with the escitalopram started in the interim and flagged as a QT safety issue.

7/13/2022. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141/min (RR 402-454 ms, coefficient of variation 0.02) with a reproducible atrial deflection preceding every QRS at a fixed interval of about 130 ms (beat-to-beat correlation of the pre-QRS segment 0.91) - an organised, regular supraventricular rhythm, read as sinus tachycardia. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about 0 to +5 degrees (normal), QT 267 ms at a median RR of 426 ms giving QTc about 409 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 380-824 ms, RMSSD 190 ms, no P waves), so the atrial fibrillation has resolved and organised rhythm has been restored.

5/12/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 82/min (RR 710-744 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS and a PR of about 150-160 ms. QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about +20 to +31 degrees (normal), QT 366 ms at RR 728 ms giving QTc about 429 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

7/16/2022. Regular sinus rhythm at 91/min (RR 650-666 ms) with an upright P in II and a deeply negative P in V1, PR about 170-185 ms (not beyond 200 ms). QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about -16 to +1 degrees (normal), QT 335 ms at RR 660 ms giving QTc about 413 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block; the high-frequency deflections lie within the QRS and are not pacing spikes. The prior ECG of 5/16/2021 showed sinus rhythm at 87/min with QRS 78 ms and QTc about 390 ms; no significant change.

7/17/2024. Sinus rhythm at about 59-61/min (RR 954-1196 ms) with an upright P wave in II preceding each QRS; PR about 205-218 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. The QRS is broad at about 130 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6, absent septal q waves and deep QS complexes in V1-V3 - complete left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -21 to -25 degrees (normal, borderline left). QT 449 ms at RR 982 ms gives QTc about 453 ms (appropriately prolonged for LBBB). The prior ECG of 6/3/2024 shows the same LBBB with QRS 128 ms, PR about 200 ms and QTc about 453 ms, so there is no new conduction abnormality and no significant interval change.

3/19/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 102/min (RR 580-596 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR about 135-145 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees (normal), QT 331 ms at RR 590 ms giving QTc about 431 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 3/18/2025 is essentially identical (sinus 101/min, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 424 ms); no change.

9/22/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 66/min (RR 904-932 ms) with an upright P wave in II (0.12 mV) before every QRS and a PR of about 150 ms. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about -20 to -27 degrees (normal), QT 369 ms at RR 910 ms giving QTc about 387 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

4/27/2022. Regular rhythm at 58/min (RR 970-1100 ms) with a low-amplitude but reproducible upright P wave in II and a negative P in V1 preceding each QRS; PR about 195-205 ms (borderline, not clearly beyond 200 ms). QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +21 to +34 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a very late broad T wave: QT 572 ms at RR 1042 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 561 ms. No bundle branch block. The prior ECG of 4/6/2022 showed atrial fibrillation (RR 324-616 ms, no P waves, rate about 130/min) with a QTc of about 446 ms. Sinus rhythm has therefore been restored (atrial fibrillation resolved) and the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms, consistent with amiodarone.

5/1/2022. Regular rhythm at 107/min (RR 554-564 ms) with a well-formed upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) and biphasic P in V1 before every QRS, PR about 155-170 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +45 to +52 degrees (normal), QT 316 ms at RR 560 ms giving QTc about 422 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 7/27/2019 showed sinus rhythm at 75/min with QRS 68 ms and QTc about 419 ms; apart from the faster rate there is no significant change.

4/19/2024. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 121/min (RR 492-502 ms) with a discrete upright P wave in II/aVF preceding each QRS at a PR of about 130 ms - sinus tachycardia (the P wave partly merges with the preceding T wave at this rate). QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +66 degrees (normal), QT 289 ms at RR 496 ms giving QTc about 410 ms. No conduction block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

8/23/2021 (10:07). Sinus rhythm at 102/min, RR 574-610 ms, upright P in II (0.16 mV) with PR about 145 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +58 degrees (normal), QT 319 ms at RR 592 ms giving QTc about 414 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (rate 100/min, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 410 ms); no change.

10/24/2024. Regular rhythm at 52/min (RR 1144-1178 ms) with a small upright P wave in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 155 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 88 ms with prominent voltage in V4-V6, frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal), QT 431 ms at RR 1160 ms giving QTc about 401 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (sinus 58/min with one premature beat, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 396 ms) there is no significant change.

12/5/2024 (14:38). Very regular rhythm at 122/min (RR 492-496 ms) with upright P waves in I/II/aVF and a negative P in V1, PR about 120 ms - sinus tachycardia. Generalised low voltage: net QRS is about -0.02 mV in lead I and +0.07 mV in aVF, giving a frontal axis of roughly +110 to +140 degrees, i.e. right axis deviation. QRS duration 90 ms, QT 295 ms at RR 494 ms giving QTc about 420 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (1:33 am), which showed a complete right bundle branch block (QRS about 148 ms with rSR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6), the QRS is now narrow and the RBBB pattern has resolved (rate-related/transient aberrancy).

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62/min (RR 944-982 ms) with upright P in II/aVF and negative P in V1, PR about 160 ms. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +45 to +65 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a long flat ST segment and a late broad T wave: QT 533 ms at RR 968 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 542 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025) had a QTc of about 411 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

9/17/2024. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant is currently ordered: the brief inpatient dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban orders all ended in January-February 2025 and current outpatient medications are only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027, continuous since 10/2/2023) at a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised for QT safety. Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 491 ms and RR 856 ms, Bazett QTc about 531 ms, compared with about 411 ms before citalopram (6/17/2020). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) is a current order (6/17/2026-1/6/2027) and has been continuous since 2022. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 572 ms and RR 1042 ms, Bazett QTc about 561 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold (the 4/6/2022 tracing in atrial fibrillation had a QTc of about 446 ms). Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal, so amiodarone is the likely cause. Prescriber review is required; a current ECG would also be reasonable given how old the last tracing is.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 11/10/2025. Because the start date is on/after 9/1/2025 but before 3/1/2026, the original memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was obtained on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG shows QTc about 542 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, satisfying the requirement (sinus rhythm, QTc about 459 ms).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 3/2/2026. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, meeting the requirement (sinus rhythm, QTc about 375 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 4/10/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. No ECG was obtained within that window; the only tracing (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start, i.e. outside the required time. The requirement was therefore not met by its due date, which has long passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/1/2026 (the only earlier exposure was a brief peri-operative inpatient order in December 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. Her only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025; no tracing has been obtained since the start, and the due date passed before the 9/24/2026 review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/10/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG exists in the clinic record, but the 8/25/2026 telephone note reports that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025), but as of the 9/24/2026 review the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/1/2026 the clinician documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR', and a new warfarin order was written the same day. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a dose change, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with documented paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation (coded AF conditions and 'paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, atrial fibrillation' in every clinic note through 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy = 1, essential hypertension = 1); age <65 and no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease. Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the only warfarin orders were brief inpatient courses in March and June 2025; current outpatient medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD - permitted to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a dose change, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is from 6/17/2026 (2.7); no INR has been resulted since the dose change and the due date passed one week before the 9/24/2026 review.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and listed in the cardiology clinic history at every visit through 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1). Anticoagulation is recommended, but no anticoagulant has ever been prescribed - current medications are levothyroxine (and previously tamsulosin) only. The prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (2025 admission) should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulant with a CHA2DS2-VASc of 3 needs review.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2, female 1). She has a very high stroke risk yet no anticoagulant: current medications are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine; the only antithrombotic ever ordered was clopidogrel in March 2025, which is not adequate for AF-related stroke prevention.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (valid through 1/4/2027) and remains current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting/continuing an anticoagulant after a major GI bleed that was explicitly held 'pending cardiology review' requires prescriber review.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was 'switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage', and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026); however rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and was never stopped, and the note's own medication list contains both apixaban and rivaroxaban. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban (plus clopidogrel) carries a major bleeding risk and must be reconciled.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves at a ventricular rate of about 132-136/min (RR intervals 346-718 ms and 348-650 ms) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, matching her coded 'unspecified atrial fibrillation'. Neither the rhythm nor the rate documented in the note is supported by the same-day tracings.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) is a current order (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 487 ms and RR 880 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. The 5/14/2024 note calling that tracing 'QT acceptable' is not supported by the tracing. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 3/18/2026) are essentially normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, started 11/10/2025 and currently ordered 7/12/2026-1/9/2027) in a man also on warfarin, clopidogrel and aspirin. His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 533 ms with RR 968 ms, Bazett QTc about 542 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold, and markedly increased from the QTc of about 411 ms on the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

interpretations.explanation: Cardiology-clinic ECG of 3/7/2026. Regular P wave before every QRS, upright in II/III/aVF and biphasic in V1, with a constant PR of about 180 ms - sinus rhythm at 81/min with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 658-856 ms). QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal), QT 323 ms with RR 744 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 375 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. The same-day clinic note stating sinus rhythm is concordant.

7/15/2025. Regular rhythm at 104/min (RR 568-586 ms) with a prominent upright P wave in II (0.22 mV) before each QRS, PR about 135 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +20 to +40 degrees (normal), QT 339 ms at RR 579 ms giving QTc about 446 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with a narrow QRS, marked ST depression and inverted T waves and a short QT (QTc of roughly 340-360 ms); the QTc is now more than 60 ms longer as the rate has slowed and the T waves have become upright.

5/21/2024. Regular rhythm at 108/min (RR 538-614 ms) with an upright P wave in II/I before each QRS and a constant PR of about 115 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal), QT 327 ms at RR 548 ms giving QTc about 442 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

6/10/2026 (19:36). Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia, RR 348-650 ms with a mean of about 440 ms (mean rate about 136/min), no organised P waves and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about 0 to +5 degrees (normal), QT 292 ms at a median RR of 418 ms giving QTc about 452 ms. The prior tracing recorded 2 hours earlier the same evening shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 132/min with an identical QRS and QTc, so there is no interval change. (Note: the clinic note of the same day describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' is contradicted by both tracings.)

8/2/2025. Very regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 864-884 ms) with a small, reproducible atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 150 ms (low-amplitude P, most visible in III/aVL; P axis is leftward/superior). QRS 72 ms, frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal), QT 397 ms at RR 872 ms giving QTc about 425 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block; the high-frequency deflections coincide with the QRS itself and are not pacing spikes. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 shows the same regular rhythm at 61/min with a QTc of about 400 ms; the QRS polarity in the limb leads is reversed on that tracing (probable arm-lead reversal), but there is no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

1/18/2021. Metronomically regular rhythm (RR 494-502 ms) at 120/min with an upright P wave in II/aVF before every QRS (0.20 mV) and a constant PR of about 160 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +48 degrees (normal), QT 274 ms with RR 498 ms giving QTc about 389 ms. No bundle branch block, no AV block. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc about 397 ms) the morphology and intervals are essentially unchanged; no significant change.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 862-902 ms), upright P in II/aVF and negative in V1 with PR about 134 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: a long flat ST segment with a late, low, broad T wave; QT 487 ms at RR 880 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 had a QTc of about 355 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms - consistent with the escitalopram started in the interim and flagged as a QT safety issue.

4/19/2024. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 121/min (RR 492-502 ms) with a discrete upright P wave in II/aVF preceding each QRS at a PR of about 130 ms - sinus tachycardia (the P wave partly merges with the preceding T wave at this rate). QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +66 degrees (normal), QT 289 ms at RR 496 ms giving QTc about 410 ms. No conduction block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

8/23/2021 (10:07). Sinus rhythm at 102/min, RR 574-610 ms, upright P in II (0.16 mV) with PR about 145 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +58 degrees (normal), QT 319 ms at RR 592 ms giving QTc about 414 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (rate 100/min, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 410 ms); no change.

10/24/2024. Regular rhythm at 52/min (RR 1144-1178 ms) with a small upright P wave in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 155 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 88 ms with prominent voltage in V4-V6, frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal), QT 431 ms at RR 1160 ms giving QTc about 401 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (sinus 58/min with one premature beat, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 396 ms) there is no significant change.

12/5/2024 (14:38). Very regular rhythm at 122/min (RR 492-496 ms) with upright P waves in I/II/aVF and a negative P in V1, PR about 120 ms - sinus tachycardia. Generalised low voltage: net QRS is about -0.02 mV in lead I and +0.07 mV in aVF, giving a frontal axis of roughly +110 to +140 degrees, i.e. right axis deviation. QRS duration 90 ms, QT 295 ms at RR 494 ms giving QTc about 420 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (1:33 am), which showed a complete right bundle branch block (QRS about 148 ms with rSR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6), the QRS is now narrow and the RBBB pattern has resolved (rate-related/transient aberrancy).

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62/min (RR 944-982 ms) with upright P in II/aVF and negative P in V1, PR about 160 ms. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +45 to +65 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a long flat ST segment and a late broad T wave: QT 533 ms at RR 968 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 542 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025) had a QTc of about 411 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

9/17/2024. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, coefficient of variation 0.28, RMSSD 249 ms) with no organised P waves - the pre-QRS segments are non-reproducible (beat-to-beat correlation 0.24) and lead II shows only a flat, low-amplitude baseline - i.e. atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 100/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms with an rS pattern in II/III/aVF and net positive QRS in I/aVL, frontal axis about -50 degrees (left axis deviation, left anterior fascicular block pattern). QT 325 ms at a median RR of 607 ms gives QTc about 417 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction/TIA 2, coronary atherosclerosis with old MI 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant is currently ordered: the brief inpatient dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban orders all ended in January-February 2025 and current outpatient medications are only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027, continuous since 10/2/2023) at a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised for QT safety. Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 491 ms and RR 856 ms, Bazett QTc about 531 ms, compared with about 411 ms before citalopram (6/17/2020). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) is a current order (6/17/2026-1/6/2027) and has been continuous since 2022. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 572 ms and RR 1042 ms, Bazett QTc about 561 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold (the 4/6/2022 tracing in atrial fibrillation had a QTc of about 446 ms). Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal, so amiodarone is the likely cause. Prescriber review is required; a current ECG would also be reasonable given how old the last tracing is.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 11/10/2025. Because the start date is on/after 9/1/2025 but before 3/1/2026, the original memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was obtained on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG shows QTc about 542 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, satisfying the requirement (sinus rhythm, QTc about 459 ms).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 3/2/2026. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, meeting the requirement (sinus rhythm, QTc about 375 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 4/10/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. No ECG was obtained within that window; the only tracing (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start, i.e. outside the required time. The requirement was therefore not met by its due date, which has long passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/1/2026 (the only earlier exposure was a brief peri-operative inpatient order in December 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. Her only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025; no tracing has been obtained since the start, and the due date passed before the 9/24/2026 review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/10/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025), but as of the 9/24/2026 review the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/1/2026 the clinician documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR', and a new warfarin order was written the same day. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a dose change, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with documented paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation (coded AF conditions and 'paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, atrial fibrillation' in every clinic note through 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy = 1, essential hypertension = 1); age <65 and no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease. Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the only warfarin orders were brief inpatient courses in March and June 2025; current outpatient medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD - permitted to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a dose change, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is from 6/17/2026 (2.7); no INR has been resulted since the dose change and the due date passed one week before the 9/24/2026 review.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and listed in the cardiology clinic history at every visit through 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1). Anticoagulation is recommended, but no anticoagulant has ever been prescribed - current medications are levothyroxine (and previously tamsulosin) only. The prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (2025 admission) should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulant with a CHA2DS2-VASc of 3 needs review.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2, female 1). She has a very high stroke risk yet no anticoagulant: current medications are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine; the only antithrombotic ever ordered was clopidogrel in March 2025, which is not adequate for AF-related stroke prevention.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (valid through 1/4/2027) and remains current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting/continuing an anticoagulant after a major GI bleed that was explicitly held 'pending cardiology review' requires prescriber review.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was 'switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage', and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026); however rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and was never stopped, and the note's own medication list contains both apixaban and rivaroxaban. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban (plus clopidogrel) carries a major bleeding risk and must be reconciled.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves at a ventricular rate of about 132-136/min (RR intervals 346-718 ms and 348-650 ms) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, matching her coded 'unspecified atrial fibrillation'. Neither the rhythm nor the rate documented in the note is supported by the same-day tracings.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) is a current order (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 487 ms and RR 880 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. The 5/14/2024 note calling that tracing 'QT acceptable' is not supported by the tracing. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 3/18/2026) are essentially normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, started 11/10/2025 and currently ordered 7/12/2026-1/9/2027) in a man also on warfarin, clopidogrel and aspirin. His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 533 ms with RR 968 ms, Bazett QTc about 542 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold, and markedly increased from the QTc of about 411 ms on the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant is currently ordered: the brief inpatient dabigatran/rivaroxaban/apixaban orders all ended in January-February 2025 and current outpatient medications are only aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin. Aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug; current order 7/15/2026-1/7/2027, continuous since 10/2/2023) at a dose above the 20 mg maximum usually advised for QT safety. Her most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 491 ms and RR 856 ms, Bazett QTc about 531 ms, compared with about 411 ms before citalopram (6/17/2020). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal. QTc >=500 ms on a watch-list drug requires prescriber review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) is a current order (6/17/2026-1/6/2027) and has been continuous since 2022. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with QT 572 ms and RR 1042 ms, Bazett QTc about 561 ms - far above the 500 ms threshold (the 4/6/2022 tracing in atrial fibrillation had a QTc of about 446 ms). Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (6/17/2026) are normal, so amiodarone is the likely cause. Prescriber review is required; a current ECG would also be reasonable given how old the last tracing is.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 11/10/2025. Because the start date is on/after 9/1/2025 but before 3/1/2026, the original memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days (by 12/10/2025). ECG 106885519 was obtained on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG shows QTc about 542 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies (due 3/14/2026). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, satisfying the requirement (sinus rhythm, QTc about 459 ms).

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 3/2/2026. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days (by 3/16/2026). ECG 104882441 was obtained on 3/7/2026, 5 days after the start, meeting the requirement (sinus rhythm, QTc about 375 ms).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 4/10/2026, so the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. No ECG was obtained within that window; the only tracing (107859369) was recorded on 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start, i.e. outside the required time. The requirement was therefore not met by its due date, which has long passed.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/1/2026 (the only earlier exposure was a brief peri-operative inpatient order in December 2025). Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. Her only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025; no tracing has been obtained since the start, and the due date passed before the 9/24/2026 review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 8/10/2026, so an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG exists in the clinic record, but the 8/25/2026 telephone note reports that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - within the required window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025), but as of the 9/24/2026 review the requirement is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit on 9/1/2026 the clinician documented 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR', and a new warfarin order was written the same day. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a dose change, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with documented paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation (coded AF conditions and 'paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, atrial fibrillation' in every clinic note through 8/4/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and cardiomyopathy = 1, essential hypertension = 1); age <65 and no diabetes, stroke or vascular disease. Score >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but the only warfarin orders were brief inpatient courses in March and June 2025; current outpatient medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline only.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD - permitted to adjust warfarin under the standing order) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily after a home INR of 3.4. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a dose change, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is from 6/17/2026 (2.7); no INR has been resulted since the dose change and the due date passed one week before the 9/24/2026 review.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded condition and listed in the cardiology clinic history at every visit through 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 1). Anticoagulation is recommended, but no anticoagulant has ever been prescribed - current medications are levothyroxine (and previously tamsulosin) only. The prior 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (2025 admission) should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulant with a CHA2DS2-VASc of 3 needs review.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis 2, female 1). She has a very high stroke risk yet no anticoagulant: current medications are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and levothyroxine; the only antithrombotic ever ordered was clopidogrel in March 2025, which is not adequate for AF-related stroke prevention.

Outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (valid through 1/4/2027) and remains current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting/continuing an anticoagulant after a major GI bleed that was explicitly held 'pending cardiology review' requires prescriber review.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was 'switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage', and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026); however rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and was never stopped, and the note's own medication list contains both apixaban and rivaroxaban. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban (plus clopidogrel) carries a major bleeding risk and must be reconciled.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves at a ventricular rate of about 132-136/min (RR intervals 346-718 ms and 348-650 ms) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, matching her coded 'unspecified atrial fibrillation'. Neither the rhythm nor the rate documented in the note is supported by the same-day tracings.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) is a current order (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 487 ms and RR 880 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. The 5/14/2024 note calling that tracing 'QT acceptable' is not supported by the tracing. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 3/18/2026) are essentially normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, started 11/10/2025 and currently ordered 7/12/2026-1/9/2027) in a man also on warfarin, clopidogrel and aspirin. His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 533 ms with RR 968 ms, Bazett QTc about 542 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold, and markedly increased from the QTc of about 411 ms on the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (6/9/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

interpretations.explanation: Cardiology-clinic ECG of 3/7/2026. Regular P wave before every QRS, upright in II/III/aVF and biphasic in V1, with a constant PR of about 180 ms - sinus rhythm at 81/min with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 658-856 ms). QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal), QT 323 ms with RR 744 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 375 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block. This is the only ECG in the chart for this patient, so there is no prior tracing for comparison. The same-day clinic note stating sinus rhythm is concordant.

7/15/2025. Regular rhythm at 104/min (RR 568-586 ms) with a prominent upright P wave in II (0.22 mV) before each QRS, PR about 135 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +20 to +40 degrees (normal), QT 339 ms at RR 579 ms giving QTc about 446 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing of 6/20/2025 showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with a narrow QRS, marked ST depression and inverted T waves and a short QT (QTc of roughly 340-360 ms); the QTc is now more than 60 ms longer as the rate has slowed and the T waves have become upright.

5/21/2024. Regular rhythm at 108/min (RR 538-614 ms) with an upright P wave in II/I before each QRS and a constant PR of about 115 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal), QT 327 ms at RR 548 ms giving QTc about 442 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

6/10/2026 (19:36). Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia, RR 348-650 ms with a mean of about 440 ms (mean rate about 136/min), no organised P waves and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response. No measurable PR interval. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about 0 to +5 degrees (normal), QT 292 ms at a median RR of 418 ms giving QTc about 452 ms. The prior tracing recorded 2 hours earlier the same evening shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 132/min with an identical QRS and QTc, so there is no interval change. (Note: the clinic note of the same day describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' is contradicted by both tracings.)

8/2/2025. Very regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69/min (RR 864-884 ms) with a small, reproducible atrial deflection preceding each QRS at a fixed interval of about 150 ms (low-amplitude P, most visible in III/aVL; P axis is leftward/superior). QRS 72 ms, frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal), QT 397 ms at RR 872 ms giving QTc about 425 ms. No bundle branch block and no AV block; the high-frequency deflections coincide with the QRS itself and are not pacing spikes. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 shows the same regular rhythm at 61/min with a QTc of about 400 ms; the QRS polarity in the limb leads is reversed on that tracing (probable arm-lead reversal), but there is no rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

5/23/2024. Regular rhythm at 98/min (RR 596-628 ms) with upright P waves in II (0.17 mV) and negative P in V1 before every QRS, PR about 115 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +4 degrees (normal), QT 307 ms at RR 616 ms giving QTc about 391 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

12/25/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 72/min (RR 820-840 ms) with a low-amplitude upright P wave in I/II before each QRS and a PR of about 135 ms. QRS 80 ms, frontal axis about +20 degrees (normal), QT 372 ms at RR 832 ms giving QTc about 408 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

11/15/2024. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 694-1164 ms, RMSSD 288 ms) with no P waves - the pre-QRS segment is flat and non-reproducible between beats (correlation -0.07) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with a controlled/slow ventricular response, mean rate about 61/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +25 degrees (normal), QT 417 ms at a median RR of 1128 ms giving QTc about 392 ms. The prior tracing of 11/12/2024 showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves (0.21 mV in II) and a PR of about 175 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new since that study; intervals are otherwise unchanged.

3/9/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 58/min (RR 976-1082 ms) with tall upright P waves in II/aVF and a PR of about 110-115 ms. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal), QT 422 ms at RR 1030 ms giving QTc about 416 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 is essentially identical (sinus 62/min, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 437 ms); no significant change.

8/23/2025. Very regular sinus rhythm at 83/min (RR 716-726 ms) with an upright P wave in II before every QRS and a PR of about 140 ms. QRS 68 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees (normal), QT 333 ms at RR 720 ms giving QTc about 393 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

6/19/2020. Regular sinus rhythm at 76/min (RR 774-804 ms) with prominent upright P waves in II (0.26 mV) and a PR of about 155 ms. QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +65 degrees (normal), QT 400 ms at RR 783 ms giving QTc about 452 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 2/2/2020 (sinus 75/min, QRS 74 ms, flat/inverted T waves with QTc about 505 ms) the T waves are now upright and the QTc is about 50 ms shorter - less than the 60 ms threshold, so no significant interval change is reported.

1/18/2021. Metronomically regular rhythm (RR 494-502 ms) at 120/min with an upright P wave in II/aVF before every QRS (0.20 mV) and a constant PR of about 160 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 88 ms, frontal axis about +48 degrees (normal), QT 274 ms with RR 498 ms giving QTc about 389 ms. No bundle branch block, no AV block. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 88 ms, QTc about 397 ms) the morphology and intervals are essentially unchanged; no significant change.

10/8/2023. Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min (RR 862-902 ms), upright P in II/aVF and negative in V1 with PR about 134 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: a long flat ST segment with a late, low, broad T wave; QT 487 ms at RR 880 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 had a QTc of about 355 ms, so the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms - consistent with the escitalopram started in the interim and flagged as a QT safety issue.

4/19/2024. Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 121/min (RR 492-502 ms) with a discrete upright P wave in II/aVF preceding each QRS at a PR of about 130 ms - sinus tachycardia (the P wave partly merges with the preceding T wave at this rate). QRS 76 ms, frontal axis about +66 degrees (normal), QT 289 ms at RR 496 ms giving QTc about 410 ms. No conduction block. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

8/23/2021 (10:07). Sinus rhythm at 102/min, RR 574-610 ms, upright P in II (0.16 mV) with PR about 145 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +58 degrees (normal), QT 319 ms at RR 592 ms giving QTc about 414 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same morning and is essentially identical (rate 100/min, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 410 ms); no change.

10/24/2024. Regular rhythm at 52/min (RR 1144-1178 ms) with a small upright P wave in II preceding each QRS at a PR of about 155 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 88 ms with prominent voltage in V4-V6, frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal), QT 431 ms at RR 1160 ms giving QTc about 401 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Compared with the prior ECG of 5/22/2023 (sinus 58/min with one premature beat, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 396 ms) there is no significant change.

12/5/2024 (14:38). Very regular rhythm at 122/min (RR 492-496 ms) with upright P waves in I/II/aVF and a negative P in V1, PR about 120 ms - sinus tachycardia. Generalised low voltage: net QRS is about -0.02 mV in lead I and +0.07 mV in aVF, giving a frontal axis of roughly +110 to +140 degrees, i.e. right axis deviation. QRS duration 90 ms, QT 295 ms at RR 494 ms giving QTc about 420 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (1:33 am), which showed a complete right bundle branch block (QRS about 148 ms with rSR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6), the QRS is now narrow and the RBBB pattern has resolved (rate-related/transient aberrancy).

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62/min (RR 944-982 ms) with upright P in II/aVF and negative P in V1, PR about 160 ms. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +45 to +65 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a long flat ST segment and a late broad T wave: QT 533 ms at RR 968 ms gives a Bazett QTc of about 542 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (before amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025) had a QTc of about 411 ms, so the QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

9/17/2024. Irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1070 ms, coefficient of variation 0.28, RMSSD 249 ms) with no organised P waves - the pre-QRS segments are non-reproducible (beat-to-beat correlation 0.24) and lead II shows only a flat, low-amplitude baseline - i.e. atrial fibrillation with a mean ventricular rate of about 100/min. No measurable PR interval. QRS 76 ms with an rS pattern in II/III/aVF and net positive QRS in I/aVL, frontal axis about -50 degrees (left axis deviation, left anterior fascicular block pattern). QT 325 ms at a median RR of 607 ms gives QTc about 417 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison.

arguments.explanation: 6/23/2025. Regular sinus rhythm at 55/min (RR 1074-1116 ms). An upright P wave precedes every QRS but the PR interval is prolonged at about 210-220 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 80 ms (deep Q waves inferiorly with a dominant R in V1-V2), frontal axis about +10 to +40 degrees (normal), QT 391 ms at RR 1103 ms giving QTc about 372 ms. No bundle branch block; the high-frequency deflections coincide with the R peak and are QRS-related, not pacing spikes. The prior tracing of 11/30/2024 is similar (sinus 51/min, PR about 185 ms, QRS 82 ms, QTc about 356 ms); no significant change.

QRS duration 90 ms, QT 295 ms at RR 494 ms giving QTc about 420 ms. Compared with the tracing from earlier the same day (1:33 am), which showed a complete right bundle branch block (QRS about 148 ms with rSR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6), the QRS is now narrow and the RBBB pattern has resolved (rate-related/transient aberrancy).

11/24/2025. Sinus rhythm at 62/min (RR 944-982 ms) with upright P in II/aVF and negative P in V1, PR about 160 ms. QRS 94 ms, frontal axis about +45 to +65 degrees (normal). 9/17/2024. Nevertheless apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (valid through 1/4/2027) and remains current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel. Restarting/continuing an anticoagulant after a major GI bleed that was explicitly held 'pending cardiology review' requires prescriber review.

Two direct oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology visit the plan was 'switching anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage', and apixaban 5 mg twice daily was started (order valid 7/15/2026-12/23/2026); however rivaroxaban 20 mg daily was re-ordered the same day (valid 7/15/2026-1/3/2027) and was never stopped, and the note's own medication list contains both apixaban and rivaroxaban. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban (plus clopidogrel) carries a major bleeding risk and must be reconciled.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves at a ventricular rate of about 132-136/min (RR intervals 346-718 ms and 348-650 ms) - i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, matching her coded 'unspecified atrial fibrillation'. Neither the rhythm nor the rate documented in the note is supported by the same-day tracings.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) is a current order (7/18/2026-12/26/2026, continuously refilled since 5/14/2024). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 487 ms and RR 880 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms - at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. The 5/14/2024 note calling that tracing 'QT acceptable' is not supported by the tracing. Most recent potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 3/18/2026) are essentially normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven. Prescriber review required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug, started 11/10/2025 and currently ordered 7/12/2026-1/9/2027) in a man also on warfarin, clopidogrel and aspirin. His most recent ECG (11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 533 ms with RR 968 ms, Bazett QTc about 542 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold, and markedly increased from the QTc of about 411 ms on the pre-amiodarone tracing of 6/7/2025.
